gonarthrose.name: Knee osteoarthritis
gonarthrose.whatYouFeel: Pain when walking and on stairs, stiffness on getting up that eases within a few minutes, knee sometimes swollen.
gonarthrose.whatHappens: The cartilage between the femur and the tibia thins, most often on the inner side, and the bone remodels. Regular activity and thigh strengthening reduce the pain.
gonarthrose.whoIsAffected: Mostly over 50, after an old knee injury, with excess weight.
gonarthrose.warning: Emergency the same day: a red, hot, very swollen knee, especially with fever or after a puncture or a wound, may be infected. Locked knee: see a doctor promptly. Swollen, hot and painful calf: get urgent medical care.

sfp.name: Patellofemoral pain syndrome
sfp.commonName: Pain at the front of the knee
sfp.whatYouFeel: Pain around or behind the kneecap on stairs, when squatting, or after sitting for long with the knees bent.
sfp.whatHappens: The kneecap slides in a groove at the front of the femur. When the load exceeds what the joint tolerates, the area becomes painful without any visible damage.
sfp.whoIsAffected: Teenagers and active adults, runners, more often women.
sfp.warning: Knee that swells, locks or gives way: see a doctor. In a child or teenager, a limp or pain spreading to the groin or thigh should be seen by a doctor promptly: the hip may be involved.

menisque.name: Medial meniscus tear
menisque.whatYouFeel: Pain on the inner edge of the knee when squatting or pivoting, sometimes catching or swelling.
menisque.whatHappens: The meniscus is a crescent-shaped cushion between the femur and the tibia. Its back part, on the inner side, is the one that tears most often. After 40, rehabilitation is the first-line treatment: arthroscopic surgery does no better.
menisque.whoIsAffected: Athletes after a twist with the knee bent, or over 40 through wear, sometimes without injury.
menisque.warning: Locked knee that cannot be straightened fully: see a doctor promptly.

pes.name: Pes anserine tendinopathy and bursitis
pes.commonName: Pain below the knee, inner side
pes.whatYouFeel: Pain a few centimetres below the joint line, on the inner face of the tibia, when climbing stairs or standing up.
pes.whatHappens: Three tendons attach together at the top of the tibia. The bursa that separates them from the medial collateral ligament and the tibia can become inflamed.
pes.whoIsAffected: Runners, breaststroke swimmers, people with knee arthritis.
pes.warning: No improvement after 6 weeks: see a doctor.

rotulien.name: Patellar tendinopathy
rotulien.whatYouFeel: Pinpoint pain below the tip of the kneecap, when jumping, landing and on stairs, tender to the touch.
rotulien.whatHappens: The patellar tendon links the kneecap to the tibia and transmits the force of the quadriceps. Its attachment below the kneecap becomes painful as jumps add up.
rotulien.whoIsAffected: Jumping and running sports: volleyball, basketball, athletics.
rotulien.warning: Sudden pain with inability to straighten the leg: get urgent medical care.

osgood.name: Osgood-Schlatter disease
osgood.commonName: Painful bump below the knee in teenagers
osgood.whatYouFeel: Tender bump below the knee, painful when running, jumping and kneeling.
osgood.whatHappens: The patellar tendon pulls on the growth cartilage of the tibia, which becomes irritated. It goes away when growth ends.
osgood.whoIsAffected: Teenage athletes going through a growth spurt, between 10 and 15.
osgood.warning: Adapt sport without stopping it completely. See a doctor promptly if the child limps, has pain at night or at rest, has a fever, if the knee is swollen or if the pain also involves the groin or thigh: a hip condition can be felt in the knee.

baker.name: Popliteal cyst
baker.whatYouFeel: Swelling and tightness at the back of the knee, difficulty bending fully.
baker.whatHappens: Fluid from the joint collects in a bursa at the back of the knee. The cyst usually reflects a problem inside the knee.
baker.whoIsAffected: Over 40, often with arthritis or a meniscus tear.
baker.warning: Swollen, red and painful calf: get urgent medical care to rule out a blood clot.

tfl.name: Iliotibial band syndrome
tfl.commonName: Runner's knee on the outer side
tfl.whatYouFeel: Pain on the outer side of the knee that appears after a few kilometres, worse downhill, and forces you to stop.
tfl.whatHappens: The iliotibial band passes over the bony bump on the outside of the femur. The area beneath it becomes irritated when the knee bends and straightens repeatedly around 30°.
tfl.whoIsAffected: Runners and cyclists, often after an increase in training volume.
tfl.warning: Pain that persists at rest or a swollen knee: see a doctor.

lcm.name: Medial collateral ligament sprain
lcm.commonName: Sprain on the inner side of the knee
lcm.whatYouFeel: Pain on the inner side of the knee after an injury, tender to the touch, sometimes a feeling that the knee opens up.
lcm.whatHappens: This broad ligament links the femur to the tibia on the inner face of the knee. In most cases it heals well without surgery.
lcm.whoIsAffected: Contact and pivoting sports, skiing, after a blow to the outer side of the knee.
lcm.warning: Get an X-ray quickly if you cannot take four steps, if pressing on the kneecap or the head of the fibula hurts, if the knee does not bend to 90°, or if you are over 55. Knee that swells a lot within hours, or feels unstable: see a doctor.

lca.name: Anterior cruciate ligament tear
lca.whatYouFeel: A pop during a twist, the knee swells within hours, then a feeling that the knee gives way.
lca.whatHappens: The anterior cruciate ligament, in the centre of the knee, stops the tibia from sliding forward under the femur. Once torn, it does not heal on its own, but rehabilitation is enough for some people.
lca.whoIsAffected: Pivoting sports: football, skiing, handball, more often women at the same level of play.
lca.warning: After a twist with a pop and rapid swelling: see a doctor within the week. X-ray first if you cannot take four steps or bend the knee to 90°. In the meantime, use crutches if needed and avoid pivoting, jumping and sport: each episode of giving way can damage the meniscus and cartilage. Balance on one leg comes later, on advice.

prerot.name: Prepatellar bursitis
prerot.commonName: Swollen knee in front of the kneecap
prerot.whatYouFeel: Soft swelling in front of the kneecap, uncomfortable when kneeling.
prerot.whatHappens: A bursa slides between the skin and the kneecap. Repeated friction fills it with fluid.
prerot.whoIsAffected: Jobs on the knees: tilers, plumbers, gardeners.
prerot.warning: Red, hot, painful area, or fever: see a doctor promptly, the bursa may become infected.

quadri.name: Quadriceps tendinopathy
quadri.whatYouFeel: Pain at the upper edge of the kneecap when squatting, climbing stairs, jumping.
quadri.whatHappens: The quadriceps tendon attaches on the upper edge of the kneecap. This attachment becomes painful when it is overloaded.
quadri.whoIsAffected: Jumping sports, weightlifting, more often over 40.
quadri.warning: Sudden pain with inability to straighten the leg: get urgent medical care.

chaise.name: Wall sit
chaise.how: Back against the wall, knees bent to 45°, without sharp pain. Hold 30 s, 4 times.

pont.name: Glute bridge
pont.how: Lying down, knees bent, lift the pelvis. 3 sets of 12.

abd.name: Side-lying leg raise
abd.how: Top leg straight, lift slowly. 3 sets of 10.
abd.videoSearch: side lying hip abduction gluteus medius

lever.name: Sit to stand
lever.how: Without using your hands if possible, lower slowly. 3 sets of 10.
lever.videoSearch: sit to stand exercise knee arthritis

ext.name: Seated knee extension
ext.how: Sitting, straighten the leg and hold 3 s. 3 sets of 12.

velo.name: Cycling or walking
velo.how: 20 to 30 minutes, 3 to 5 times a week, at an acceptable level of pain.

isoq.name: Quad set with the leg straight
isoq.how: Lying down, press the knee down into the bed, hold 5 s. 3 sets of 10.

talon.name: Heel slide
talon.how: Lying down, bend then straighten the knee by sliding the heel. 15 times.

squatdec.name: Single-leg decline squat
squatdec.how: Lower over 3 s on the painful leg, come back up on both legs. 3 sets of 15.

isotend.name: Knee extension hold against resistance
isotend.how: Sitting, knee at 60°, push against a strap without moving. Hold 45 s, 5 times.

planche.name: Side plank
planche.how: Resting on the forearm, pelvis in line. Hold 20 to 40 s, 3 times each side.

etfl.name: Tensor fasciae latae stretch
etfl.how: Leg crossed behind, lean the trunk to the other side. 3 times 30 s.
etfl.videoSearch: tensor fasciae latae IT band stretch

equi.name: Single-leg balance
equi.how: Knee slightly bent, 3 times 30 s, then on a cushion.

ischio.name: Knee bend against a band
ischio.how: Lying face down or standing, bring the heel towards the buttock. 3 sets of 12.

etisch.name: Hamstring stretch
etisch.how: Lying down, leg straight towards the ceiling, held behind the thigh. 3 times 30 s.

etquad.name: Quadriceps stretch
etquad.how: Standing or lying on your side, heel towards the buttock, pelvis neutral. 3 times 30 s.

glace.name: Protect and relieve
glace.how: Avoid kneeling, ice for 15 minutes 2 to 3 times a day during a flare-up.
